· **Evidence slot:** 4 — telemetry (KSI-MLA, CA-7 / SI-4) · **Track modules:** [A4](../compliance-track.html#module-a4-telemetry-control-plane-slot-4), [B5](../implementation-track.html#module-b5-detect-protect-books-0810)

## Scope

Closes the "payload gap" left after network/identity hardening: the pipe is
regulated but the content is opaque. A federal CUI classification taxonomy
enforced via Purview sensitivity labels, DLP across three enforcement
surfaces, and agency-controlled cryptographic key management in Azure Key
Vault. **Both pipe and payload controls are required for FedRAMP
Moderate.**

## Learning objectives

- Explain why CASB/network controls alone cannot prevent exfiltration of
  unclassified-but-sensitive content.
- Map the federal CUI framework (EO 13556, NARA CUI Registry) — Public,
  Internal, CUI-Basic, CUI-Specified — to a parent/child Purview label
  taxonomy created via Security & Compliance PowerShell.
- Build automatic labeling with pre-built and custom Sensitive Information
  Types and trainable classifiers, deployed in simulation mode first.
- Implement the DLP baseline across service-layer
  (SharePoint/OneDrive/Exchange/Teams), Endpoint DLP (print/USB/clipboard/
  upload), and CASB network-layer surfaces.
- Deploy Key Vault Premium (HSM, FIPS 140-2 Level 2) with CMK for SQL TDE
  and SharePoint BYOK, Managed Identity RBAC, and a 12-month rotation
  policy.
- Distinguish AU-12 (audit generation) from AU-10 (non-repudiation) and
  configure Purview Audit Premium tiered retention.
- Structure a Certificate Practice Statement per RFC 3647 (SC-17).

## Key concepts

- Four-tier CUI label taxonomy with escalating protections.
- The Purview-labels-feed-the-CASB integration pattern (payload signal for
  network enforcement).
- Three DLP enforcement surfaces; custom SITs; trainable classifiers
  (50–500 samples).
- Four-level key hierarchy: offline root CA HSM → issuing CA in Key Vault
  → CMK → wrapped DEKs.
- Audit Premium events: MailItemsAccessed, SearchQueryInitiated,
  SensitivityLabel* (downgrade detection).
- Infoblox IPAM/DNS underpinning CRL/OCSP reliability.

## Implementation sequence

1. Create and publish the four-tier label taxonomy to all locations.
2. Build custom SITs and trainable classifiers; auto-labeling in
   simulation → review → enforce.
3. Deploy service-layer DLP baseline (block external share/send of CUI).
4. Verify Defender for Endpoint onboarding, then deploy Endpoint DLP.
5. Create Key Vault Premium (soft-delete, purge protection, RBAC); mint
   HSM CMKs.
6. Migrate SQL TDE protector to CMK; automatic rotation (P12M).
7. Enable Audit Premium with tiered retention (10-year privileged /
   1-year default).
8. Author the CPS per RFC 3647; verify CRL/OCSP reachability.

## Compliance hooks

AC-4, AU-10, MP-2, MP-3, MP-4, MP-5, SC-12, SC-12(1), SC-13, SC-17,
SC-28. NIST SP 800-171, SP 800-57 Part 1, FIPS 140-2 Level 2, NARA CUI
Marking Handbook, RFC 3647. FedRAMP 20x KSIs: data protection, key
management, non-repudiation, boundary protection.

## Prerequisites

Books 01–08: PKI (01), SASE/CASB (02), Conditional Access (01–03), SQL
TDE (04–05), PAM (07), SIEM context (08/10). Security & Compliance
PowerShell and Az modules.

## Labs

1. Build the label taxonomy and an auto-labeling policy in simulation
   mode; seed SharePoint with SSN-containing test docs; review the
   simulation report for false positives before enforcing.
2. Create a custom SIT with keyword corroboration and a DLP rule blocking
   external email of matching content; verify the policy tip.
3. Stand up Key Vault Premium, migrate an Azure SQL TDE protector to CMK,
   apply a rotation policy, and confirm key operations in Log Analytics.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- Publishing labels to only one location causes inconsistent
  classification — publish everywhere from day one.
- Enforcing auto-labeling without a simulation review can mislabel at
  scale and flood the help desk.
- Trainable classifiers trained on unrepresentative samples underperform
  (budget 3–4 weeks).
- Endpoint DLP silently misses devices not onboarded to Defender for
  Endpoint; never delete a compromised key version until data is
  re-encrypted.
